landmarks.name: Gorongosa National Park
landmarks.writeup: A biodiversity hotspot known for its wildlife and scenic landscapes, crucial for conservation efforts.

landmarks.name: Island of Mozambique
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site featuring colonial architecture and historical significance as a former Portuguese trading post.

landmarks.name: Bazaruto Archipelago
landmarks.writeup: A group of islands famous for pristine beaches, coral reefs, and marine biodiversity.

cultural_events.name: Mozambique Independence Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on June 25th, marking independence from Portugal in 1975 with parades and cultural performances.

cultural_events.name: Maputo International Music Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event showcasing local and international music, promoting cultural exchange.

food_writeup: Mozambican cuisine blends African, Portuguese, and Arab influences, featuring dishes like peri-peri chicken, seafood, cassava, and matapa, a stew made with cassava leaves and peanuts.
brief_history: Mozambique was a Portuguese colony until 1975 when it gained independence. The country experienced a civil war from 1977 to 1992 but has since been rebuilding and developing its economy.

important_people.name: Joaquim Chissano
important_people.description: Second President who helped bring peace

current_conflicts: Mozambique faces ongoing insurgency in the northern Cabo Delgado province, involving Islamist militant groups causing humanitarian and security challenges.
